lesson_title: Why Your Potjie Pot Is Iron
hook_text: Why is a potjie pot made of heavy iron and not light plastic? Every material is chosen for a reason.
clip_script: A potjie pot sits right in the coals. Plastic would melt into a puddle. Iron melts only at about one and a half thousand degrees. That is a high melting point. Iron also carries heat from the coals and spreads it evenly through the stew: a good heat conductor. So why do we stir it with a wooden spoon? Because wood is an insulator. It keeps the heat away from your hand. Same idea in your phone charger: copper inside to carry electricity, plastic outside to keep it from you. Now a trick question: is glass strong? It is hard, it resists scratches, but drop it and it shatters. Brittle. And why are aeroplanes aluminium, not steel? Strong enough, but almost three times lighter. Pick the material that fits every part of the job.
visual_style: Whiteboard potjie pot on coals with a thermometer; a wooden spoon and a metal spoon side by side, one glowing; a dropped glass shattering; an aeroplane on a scale beside a steel block.
mood: Practical and a little bit braai-day fun.
pacing: Warm opener, quick property-by-property reveals, a punchy aeroplane finish.
